maya: Pasting an nsys trace snapshot — I'm seeing repeated short memcpy bursts that appear to serialize kernels on stream 7. timeline: https://traces/reports/2178902468 (redacted)
maya: Memcpy spans ~200us, kernel launches are ~400us, but there's a ~350-700us CPU gap between memcpy completion and kernel launch on the same stream :thinking:
tom: Can you paste the nsys waterfall view? Is the memcpy host->device pinned memory or pageable copy? That affects async overlap.
maya: It's using cuMemcpyAsync from our pinned pool (we're using pinned allocator for prefetch). Screenshot shows H2D on stream 7 then kernel A on stream 7, but kernels on other streams overlap with the memcpy — only same-stream kernels wait.
anil: Sounds like stream serialization (implicit dependency) or cudaStreamSynchronize somewhere. Any host-side sync in the path after enqueue? e.g., calling cudaDeviceSynchronize or reading event statuses?
maya: I grepped — no explicit sync in the hot path. We do set device flags once at startup. Batcher code:

```cpp
// in prefetcher
cudaMemcpyAsync(dst, src, len, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice, stream);
// then record a small event
cudaEventRecord(prefetch_evt, stream);
// later kernel is launched on same stream after some host-side AVX work
```

maya: The odd part is CPU scheduling gaps: nsys shows the thread doing ~200us of Python-side prep, then idle for ~400us before kernel launch. That idle corresponds to a different user thread on the core getting scheduled.
lee: Could be OS preemption of the host thread that decides when to submit the kernel (enqueue). If batching heuristic yields large host-side prep, we might be hitting scheduler slices. Are we pinning the submitter thread to a high-priority core?
tom: We have a submitter pinned in dedicated infra, but on some repro boxes it's not. Also our prefetcher uses std::this_thread::sleep_for in backoff which can drop scheduling priority.
anil: Another angle: NVTX ranges in the trace — do memcpy ranges include the transfer endpoint? If the memcpy is async but the host later touches the backing pages, that triggers implicit sync. Check for touching 'src' after enqueue.
maya: Good call — prefetcher touches a checksum field in the buffer after enqueue (bug!). That could fault and serialize. I'll instrument.
perf-bot: Automated perf diff: recent rollout 2026-03-10 introduced prefetch checksum change (commit 9f3b). Regression +3.8% p50 latency on short seq (S=64). Suspect host-touch -> page fault.
lee: If it's a page fault, we'd see the memcpy block earlier in the trace? nsys might show CPU 'page fault' activity; check syscall view for mprotect/munmap/faults.
maya: Added a quick build removing the checksum touch — local nsys shows overlap restored, same-stream kernel now launches immediately after memcpy completes without extra host gap. Preliminary: p50 down ~4%.
tom: Nice. Action items:
- maya: open PR to remove checksum touch and add test ensuring prefetcher doesn't touch pages after async enqueue
- anil: add NVTX markers around prefetch path and a lightweight perf-test to catch regressions
- lee: investigate submitter thread affinity and replace sleep_for backoff with condition_variable
maya: I'll start the PR and attach the reduced repro trace. Thanks :thumbsup:
anil: Also let's add a CI nsys smoke that runs replay on small seqs and flags host-side idle > 200us between memcpy complete and kernel launch on same stream.
perf-bot: Noted. I'll create an alert rule for regressions matching 'host enqueue gap' signature.
maya: cc @tom @anil @lee — leaving the trace link in the PR. If anyone wants the raw .nsys, DM me.
